topic: What if you brought a modern car to ancient Rome?
title: WHAT IF YOU BROUGHT A
MODERN CAR TO ANCIENT ROME?

youtube.title: What If You Brought a Modern Car to Ancient Rome?
youtube.intro: Three days after passing your driving test, you and your friend Mo drive into a tunnel and come out in Rome, in the year 113. Your car works perfectly. To the Romans it is a chariot of the gods. There is just one problem: every drop of fuel you burn is gone forever.
youtube.pinned_comment:
Give the car to the emperor or run for the tunnel? 👇 What would you do, and why?

And who do you think made those other tyre tracks? Best theory gets pinned before Part 2.

The history is real: Julius Caesar banned most carts from Rome's streets by day, the Circus Maximus held around 150,000 people, and Europe didn't distill alcohol until about the 1100s. Sources are in the description.

🔔 Subscribe so you don't miss Part 2, and find out who made those tracks.
